observed_image_control.interpretation: Different filenames can denote identical content under a raw-byte representation.

formal.I: target invariant, for R12 I_F(B)=EXISTS Y F(Y,B)
formal.R: canonical representation proven to preserve I
formal.B: bridge invariant sufficient to reach the target decision representation
formal.safe_merge: C(x)=C(y) AND preservation_proof(I,R) -> x and y may share one memoized proof/search state within the proven scope
formal.bridge_rule: R need not preserve every feature of the original state; it must preserve the bridge information required to recover/verify I
formal.full_chain: RAW_STATE -> REPRESENTATION_CONTRACT -> CANONICAL_CLASS -> BRIDGE_INTERFACE -> TERMINAL_CANDIDATE -> VERIFY

R12_instantiation.content: canonical literal set of the derived clause
R12_instantiation.quotient: all derivation histories yielding the same canonical clause are memoized as one state
R12_instantiation.target_bridge: bridge-only clauses of width <=4 describing the exact existential interface
R12_instantiation.why_sound: future resolution behavior of a clause depends on its literals, not on the filename/history by which the identical clause was obtained
R12_instantiation.limitation: This does not yet merge semantically equivalent but syntactically different clauses or formulas. Such a stronger quotient requires a separate invariant-preservation proof.

research_question: Can a polynomially computable, decision-invariant-preserving canonical representation collapse proof/search histories strongly enough that the exact bridge interface is derivable without forbidden width/search debt?
seal: DO_NOT COUNT DIFFERENT NAMES TWICE. DO NOT MERGE DIFFERENT MEANINGS ONCE.
